scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Clothes go in soaking wet, and come out of the spin cycle just damp. Where did the water go?

scenes.name: drain
scenes.text: After rinsing, the machine pumps out the loose water. But the clothes are still soaked.

scenes.name: spin
scenes.text: Then the drum speeds up, to around a thousand turns a minute or more, in many front loaders.

scenes.name: inertia
scenes.text: Anything moving in a circle tends to fly off in a straight line. That's inertia.

scenes.name: holes
scenes.text: The drum wall holds the clothes in, but water slips through its tiny holes, and drains away.

scenes.name: force
scenes.text: At full speed, the clothes feel hundreds of times the pull of gravity, squeezing water out.

scenes.name: balance
scenes.text: If clothes bunch up on one side, the drum wobbles. Sensors detect it, and the machine slows down to spread them out.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Drain, spin, inertia, holes. Water out, by physics. Follow for more on how things really work.
